title: LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
summary: LoopSpec replaces standard autoregressive decoding in Looped Transformers with a training-free self-speculative scheme in which early recurrent depths draft tokens, deeper depths optionally re-propose, and the full model verifies, pipelined so drafting overlaps verification. It costs additional implementation complexity in the decoding loop and extra compute for verification and the selective second proposal, though it requires no auxiliary draft model and no retraining. It can fail to deliver speedup if draft acceptance rates are low on the target workload, and it applies only to Looped Transformer architectures, which are not the mainstream open-weight models the reader is likely to deploy.
rationale: The method is restricted to Looped Transformers, a niche architecture the reader is unlikely to run in production, so the claim is worth tracking but not actionable on constrained infrastructure today.
technique: Pipelined self-speculative decoding for looped transformers

claims.statement: LoopSpec replaces standard autoregressive decoding in Looped Transformers with a training-free self-speculative scheme in which early recurrent depths draft tokens, deeper depths optionally re-propose, and the full model verifies, pipelined so drafting overlaps verification. It costs additional implementation complexity in the decoding loop and extra compute for verification and the selective second proposal, though it requires no auxiliary draft model and no retraining. It can fail to deliver speedup if draft acceptance rates are low on the target workload, and it applies only to Looped Transformer architectures, which are not the mainstream open-weight models the reader is likely to deploy.
The paper reports up to 6.83x inference speedup across diverse Looped Transformers on reasoning and coding benchmarks, with lossless decoding under greedy and sampling regimes.
